contexts.text: It is a universal law, that influx accommodates itself according to efflux; and if the efflux is prevented, the influx is prevented: through the internal man there is an influx of good and truth from the Lord; through the external man there ought to be an efflux into the life; that is, in the exercise of charity. When there is this efflux, the influx from Heaven is continuous... whereas if the efflux does not exist... the influx accommodates itself to the efflux... TCR 814.
It is of the Lord... from whose efflux, or Divine sphere, all these things are disposed into order.
The general efflux from Hell is against the Divine of the Lord, charity, and the holiness of the Word.
